content.text: Found it: Streamdown’s code block reserves `contain-intrinsic-size: auto 200px` with `content-visibility: auto`, so short SQL expands tall then snaps. Overriding that in `.hide-code-header`.
Dropping the inline comment to match the file's style.

Streamdown’s code blocks use `content-visibility: auto` with `contain-intrinsic-size: auto 200px`, so the browser reserves ~200px until layout finishes — short SQL then snaps down to one line (worse with the accordion open animation).

Fixed in `.hide-code-header` by forcing `content-visibility: visible` and clearing the reserved size, so query view opens at the real height.

content.text:
The earlier CSS change couldn’t win — Streamdown sets that size with **inline styles**.

Two fixes in place now:

1. **Inline Code view** — `SqlQueryDisplay` no longer uses Streamdown, so there’s no reserved ~200px height. Short queries open at their real height.
2. **Side panel** — the SQL pane had no `defaultSize`, so it took the leftover space (~400px) and then `fitSqlPanelToContent` shrank it. It now starts from an estimate of the SQL height.

Try the Code icon again (hard refresh if styles were cached). If it still jumps, say whether it’s the inline Code toggle or the side panel (pencil).
